result.summary: Acquires an exclusive file lock on the blocks directory in BlockManager using an RAII helper class. This ensures any consumer of BlockManager, including libbitcoinkernel users and utilities like bitcoin-chainstate, locks the blocks directory for its lifetime.
result.problem: Previously, only bitcoind locked the blocks directory during initialization, while the kernel did no directory locking. A kernel program pointed at a running node's blocks directory with a fresh or in-memory database would succeed, open blk00000.dat in place with read/write mode, and silently overwrite existing block files from offset 0, corrupting the running node's data.
evidence: PR description: 'with an empty block index BlockManager writes from offset 0 of the node's blk00000.dat, which FlatFileSeq::Open opens in place with "rb+". The node keeps running and serves the overwritten bytes as its own blocks.'
Referenced PR #31674 discussion: noted that 'the kernel does not currently do any dir locking, but it should', with a reviewer suggesting moving the lock into the BlockManager constructor.
result.changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the PR content; the diff and functional test are now attached.
result.card: Moves the blocks directory file lock into BlockManager using an RAII member class, ensuring kernel consumers and standalone tools lock the directory just like bitcoind. Previously, kernel consumers did not lock the blocks directory, allowing a separate process pointing at a running node's blocks directory with an empty index to overwrite blk00000.dat in place and silently corrupt block storage. This resolves an omission highlighted during the review of PR 31674, where directory locking was originally added for bitcoind.

risk.why: Failure to acquire or release the blocks directory lock could cause bitcoind or kernel applications to fail startup or reindex unexpectedly.
